NEW: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt has described the incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport as a hybrid attack scenario calling it a new level of threat for Germany.

Speaking after visiting the airport, Dobrindt said the discovery of a drone carrying an explosive device represents a new security challenge, warning that similar attacks could target airports, industrial facilities, or large public gatherings.

He stressed that investigators do not believe the device was built by amateurs, saying the drone, the explosive payload, and the overall execution indicate a high degree of technical expertise and access to sophisticated equipment.

Saxony's Interior Minister Armin Schuster also described the incident as a suspected hybrid attack, calling it an extremely serious security event and noting that this is the first known case in Germany of a drone equipped with explosives being found at an airport.

Authorities confirmed that Germany's drone defense units have been deployed to secure Leipzig/Halle Airport against any additional threats. Investigators are also searching for components that may belong to a possible second drone, while continuing forensic examinations of the recovered device.

The investigation, led by the Attorney General's Office, is now focused on identifying those responsible. Officials say all possible motives remain under investigation, including terrorism, extremism, and foreign state involvement.

Dobrindt concluded that Germany is facing an evolving technological threat, describing it as "a race or an arms race" between those developing drone attack capabilities and the authorities building systems to detect and defeat them.

The drill tested command continuity, interagency coordination, and emergency government operations.
